Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency numbers. Procurement/legal asked me to confirm a few things so we can complete our vendor risk review and get to signature:

- Can you share your current DPA and indicate whether Redwood will execute the EU SCCs + the UK Addendum (UK IDTA) for UK data?
- We need your current subprocessors (names + locations) and whether any subprocessors process customer content outside the EU/UK.
- Does Redwood have an internal TIA / DTIA for the hosted API? If so, can you provide a summary of the risk treatment controls (encryption, routing, access controls)?
- Is there a routing/profile option to keep inference traffic and logs within EU-only regions for production? If not, what mitigations do you provide?

We also need to receive SOC 2 type II or equivalent evidence; if that's not available, point us to the compliance package and attestations.

Target timeline: we want to complete the review by EOW next week (Sep 17). Any chance you can send materials and a short note on routing options by EOD tomorrow?

Best,
Elena

Appreciate the clear list. Attaching our current DPA (redwood_dpa_v3.pdf) and the latest subprocessor roster (subprocessor_list_2026Q3.csv). High-level answers below; Marcus from privacy is cc'd to confirm the legal specifics.

- DPA / SCCs / UK Addendum: We are prepared to sign the EU SCCs and execute the UK Addendum where applicable. Marcus / Legal will confirm any small redlines we usually expect on insurance and liability language.
- Subprocessors: Attached CSV includes locations. A few model-hosting subprocessors operate in the US; I’ve flagged those rows.
- TIA / DTIA: We maintain an internal TIA for hosted inference and a summarized version is attached (tia_summary_2026-09-10.pdf). It calls out encryption in-transit and at-rest, per-customer KV cache segregation, and our routing policies.
- EU-only routing: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can guarantee EU-only processing and data residency. For the hosted API (our standard offering) we route by policy (region preference) but cannot guarantee absolute EU-only physical processing unless you opt for a Dedicated pool in EU region.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Marcus to confirm UK IDTA applicability and any additional evidence Medivault wants.
2) If Medivault needs EU-only processing, we can scope Dedicated capacity pricing and a short timeline.
3) If you want the DPA executed now, confirm signatory and we’ll send via DocuSign (looping Laura).

Will follow up with Marcus shortly.

Thanks,

Elena / Kimberly —

Short version from privacy: yes, Redwood will execute the EU SCCs and we can include the UK Addendum (often called the UK IDTA) when the contracting entity indicates UK applicability. A few operational notes and options so Medivault can decide:

- Hosted API (default): model inference happens on our multi-tenant fleet. We have region-aware routing and prefer EU regions for EU customers, but we cannot contractually guarantee EU-only physical processing for the hosted tier unless you select a Dedicated commitment in the EU. If your requirement is contractual EU-only processing, Dedicated or Private is the path.
- Dedicated / Private: guarantees onshore processing in EU data centers; supports customer-managed VPC for Private.
- Subprocessors: see attached roster. The US-based subprocessors are limited to model hosting and telemetry ingestion for monitoring; we apply strict access controls, encryption, and contractual restrictions (no use beyond serving model inference).
- TIA summary: attached. Key mitigations are AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, per-tenant keys, strict RBAC for operator tools, audit logs retained for 1 year by default (extendable), and optional log redaction workflows.

Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA — we can share through the secure compliance portal once we have a point of contact. Alternatively, we can share a compliance package bundle (certs and a SOC2 summary) immediately.

If Medivault needs us to add an explicit contractual clause stating that we will not route EU-origin requests through non-EU infrastructure except for fallbacks, we can add a routing addendum; however, that would be profile-level (hosted fallback allowed) or absolute (requires Dedicated).

Action items:
- Elena: confirm whether you require absolute EU-only processing (yes/no) and the legal signatory for the DPA (name, title, email).
- Kimberly / Laura: prepare DocuSign envelope once Elena confirms.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference

If you can send an updated DPA with the routing addendum and the UK Addendum included, we’ll aim to return redlines by Sep 17. Also: can you confirm the typical latency impact if we move to Dedicated EU pool for our pilot (ballpark)?
